note: Chime (audio designer), brief 059, 2026-10-26. rivals-coming is muted (volume 0, was 0.85) on Sky's word, 2026-10-26: "just turn it off for now - I'll do a proper audio pass later" (the foghorn); the cue still fires, so proofs that read CuesPlayed are unchanged. The one place the game reads for which sound plays on which event. Clips are in unity/Assets/Suborned/Resources/Audio/ (made by tools/audio/synth.ts; their hashes are in clips.json). A cue is keyed by a sim log code; a loop by what the car does. Unity: Resources.Load<AudioClip>(clip); there is no AudioMixer asset yet, so `buses` are named gain groups the host multiplies (db) until Latch makes a mixer from them.

cues.note: timing and consequence cues: the clock's sounds, always 2D, never ducked

vehicles.note: cars on the street; 3D, heard by distance from the camera's ground focus

family.note: One cue per meaning, kept apart by register, timbre and length so no two are mistaken for each other. Reserved rows have no clip yet.

rows.meaning: the rival car turns in: they are here
rows.register: low 90-600 Hz, buzzy brass, two falling tones (D3 then B2) over a tyre swish
mid-high 600-2500 Hz, bell partials, major, long ring

rows.meaning: a watcher has noticed an agent
rows.register: high 2.5-4 kHz, one dry ping, no tail

on.at: 2:35 on the Handover; also the drawn entry (racing for the gunfire) and the late entry (F5, F6), same code, same cue

spatial.pan: optional: stereo pan toward the side of the screen the car enters from (Orbit Walk), pan = clamp(dot(cameraRight, entry - cameraFocus) / 40 m, -0.6, 0.6); no distance fade
spatial.reason: a clock cue is heard wherever the camera is; the pan says which way to look

cues.playsWhile: once, on the tick the rivals.coming log line appears, at any game speed; it is a clock cue, so it is not heard again in a replay's scrub unless the host replays the tick

loops.follows: car:rivals (the pose from Game.RivalCarPose(), world position and heading)

spatial.listener: the camera's ground focus point (the look-at point on the street), not the camera, which sits high above it

loops.playsWhile: the car is moving: its pose changed more than 0.05 m/s between frames (car.pace: 5 m/s on a carriageway, 2 m/s on a drive or in a bay). It starts on the rivals.coming tick, stops when the pose stops or is null (parked, dropping, off the map)

gain.note: volume scale and pitch rise linearly with the measured speed between those bounds; at the yard pace (2 m/s) it runs about 0.65 volume and 0.88 pitch

loops.restart: randomise the start offset on each play so it does not always start on the same beat; the same clip serves any later move (rivals.follows, rivals.back, the fight stand)
